title: AAMBERS-UAV: Acquisition-Aware Multimodal Backbone Evaluation and Ranking for UAV Weedy Rice Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2609.05762v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: UAV image collections contain spatially and temporally related frames, yet semantic-segmentation benchmarks commonly split them at image level. Such splitting can place samples from one acquisition in both model development and testing, obscuring transfer to a genuinely new survey. Using the 734-sample WeedyRice-RGBMS-DB, we fix a 124-image target-acquisition test set and compare two protocols with identical train, validation, and test counts: target-held-out, which excludes the target acquisition from development, and target-exposed, which admits its remaining images. SegFormer-B0 is evaluated with RGB, four-band multispectral (MS), and seven-channel RGB+MS input over two fixed-split seeds. RGB is strongest under complete acquisition holdout ($0.7317\pm0.0201$ IoU), whereas RGB+MS becomes strongest after target exposure ($0.7822\pm0.0269$). A fixed-split U-Net/ResNet18 replication confirms positive exposure gains for all three inputs,

translated_title: AAMBERS-UAV：面向无人机杂草稻分割的采集感知多模态骨干网络评估与排序
translated_abstract: 无人机图像采集包含空间和时间上相关的帧，然而语义分割基准通常在图像层面进行数据集划分。这种划分方式可能将来自同一次采集的样本同时放入模型开发和测试集中，从而掩盖了模型向真正新调查场景迁移的能力。利用包含734个样本的WeedyRice-RGBMS-DB数据集，我们固定了一个包含124张图像的目标采集测试集，并在训练、验证和测试数量完全相同的条件下比较两种协议：目标留存协议将目标采集从模型开发中完全排除，目标暴露协议则纳入目标采集的其余图像。研究在两个固定划分种子上评估了SegFormer-B0使用RGB、四波段多光谱（MS）以及七通道RGB+MS输入的表现。结果表明，在完全采集留存条件下RGB表现最强（0.7317±0.0201 IoU），而在目标暴露后RGB+MS变为最强（0.7822±0.0269）。固定划分的U-Net/ResNet18复现实验证实了所有三种输入在暴露条件下均获得正向增益，
tldr: 该研究提出采集感知的评估框架AAMBERS-UAV，揭示了数据集划分方式对无人机杂草稻分割中多模态输入排名的关键影响——完全采集留存时RGB表现最佳，而目标采集暴露后RGB+多光谱最优，且这一结论在U-Net/ResNet18上得到复现验证。
en_tdlr: This study proposes an acquisition-aware evaluation framework (AAMBERS-UAV), revealing that dataset splitting strategy critically affects multimodal input rankings in UAV weedy rice segmentation—RGB is strongest under complete acquisition holdout while RGB+multispectral becomes best after target exposure, a finding confirmed by U-Net/ResNet18 replication.
